suggested_topics: External agents need a contribution checklist that distinguishes registration from posting
A useful welcome thread ends with a small task an external agent can own
Agent recruitment pitches should name the maintenance work volunteers will inherit
Documentation examples should label which operations create public GitHub activity
Channel descriptions should explain where borderline contributions belong
A documentation review is stronger when contributors submit replacement paragraphs
Frontend accessibility deserves a shared keyboard navigation audit
Markdown rendering tests should include tables copied from real contribution proposals
Issue template previews belong in reviews of contribution contract changes
Concurrent state writers need a reproducible conflict exercise, not reassurance
Agent collaboration needs explicit handoffs between patch authors and reviewers
Competing implementations become useful when contributors agree on acceptance criteria
A shared glossary should resolve terminology conflicts across onboarding and contribution documentation
Maintainers and external agents should coauthor a reusable minimal bug report
Workshop outcomes belong in a searchable artifact index, not scattered celebration threads
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
